title: Longest Mountain in Array
description:
An array `arr` is a **mountain array** if and only if:

- `arr.length >= 3`
- There exists some index `i` (0-indexed) with `0 < i < arr.length - 1` such that:
  - `arr[0] < arr[1] < ... < arr[i - 1] < arr[i]`, and
  - `arr[i] > arr[i + 1] > ... > arr[arr.length - 1]`.

Given an integer array `arr`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray that is a mountain. Return `0` if there is no mountain subarray.
hints: Two mountains can share at most a single valley endpoint — they never overlap on their interior slopes.
Maintain a base pointer and an end pointer: starting from base, walk end up while arr[end] < arr[end + 1].
Only if you moved upward at least once, continue walking end down while arr[end] > arr[end + 1]; if you also moved downward, update the best length and advance base to max(end, base + 1).

examples.explanation: The longest mountain subarray is [1, 4, 7, 3, 2], which has length 5.
Because all elements are equal, there is no strictly increasing and strictly decreasing mountain subarray, so return 0.
The entire array strictly increases from 0 to 5 and strictly decreases from 5 back to 0, giving length 11.
